scope: Read-only source inspection of the supplemental two-test compiled wrapper and its dependencies. No pytest, compiler, binary or native test was executed.

checks.CXX_selection: shutil.which(os.environ.get("CXX", "c++")); one executable path/name, no shell expansion or embedded compiler flags. The outer run must select and pin the intended compiler.
checks.temporary_log_retention: Logs live under pytest tmp_path; publication/runner must retain the temporary output before cleanup.

findings.title: Timed-out compile or fixture execution does not retain its partial logs
findings.detail: Both subprocess.run calls use capture_output and timeout, but write their logs only after normal return. TimeoutExpired therefore bypasses the write_text calls and loses its captured stdout/stderr from the intended artifact directory. An executable OSError likewise leaves no attempt record. Preserve partial stdout/stderr plus exception/status before re-raising, or direct output to opened log files and retain terminal metadata.

limits: This wrapper exercises standalone C++ metadata/evaluation/serializer fixtures; it does not certify actual native Polynomial batch selection, full source installation, full trajectory closure or the frozen numerical gates.
No scientific source or repository file was changed by this review.

installer_author_test_runtime.framework: Python standard-library unittest.main(); pytest not required or invoked
installer_author_test_runtime.note: The prior author invocation used python3 directly; the current runtime readback resolves to /usr/bin/python3.14. The earlier log records 35 tests and OK but did not itself pin the interpreter.
